note: Patches applied to a pinned sibling checkout before generation, so a module the compiler refuses to lower today can still ship. A patch here may only rewrite an expression into an equivalent the compiler does lower. It may NEVER change observable behavior -- absence, reference identity, equality, ordering, exception shape, task settlement -- because the generated header is then tested against the patched source, so a behavioral patch is a lie our own tests would certify. Each patch states the equivalence that makes it safe and the refusal it answers. The patch is applied after the pin integrity check and reverted when generation ends, so the checkout is only ever dirty inside one run. `baseCommit` pins the patch to the revision it was written against: a pin move that breaks the patch fails loudly instead of silently applying to different code.

patches.equivalence: The package exports only its root and contract entry points, neither of which re-exports these internal types. A type-only internal export and local annotations emit no JavaScript, make the same call once, retain the same reference, and perform the same reads in the same order.
patches.whyNotUpstreamFirst: The source inference is already exact in TypeScript, but the pinned C++ emitter re-derives use-site anonymous rows when a return interface is private to another module. Naming that internal interface supplies target-neutral evidence without changing the package API or runtime behavior.
patches.verification: Targeted regeneration of @flighthq/path emitted every module with the patch applied, and all 31 package headers compiled independently. The annotation-only ReturnType spelling was measured first, remained 26/31, and was removed.
patches.unblocks: Makes stroke_path.hpp, tessellate_stroke_path.hpp, and explain_stroke_path_tessellation.hpp compile, clearing their two aggregator cascades and moving @flighthq/path from 26/31 to 31/31.
patches.expires: when the emitter retains a call expression's declared nominal return owner through local inference, or Flight adopts the explicit annotations.

patches.refusal: object-literal diagnostic details are emitted as a brace initializer that cannot cross both Record and optional<Record> construction boundaries
patches.rewrite: Binds each diagnostic detail object to its already-declared Record<string, boolean | number | string> parameter type before passing it, and binds the nullable output length to an explicitly numeric local.
patches.equivalence: The binding evaluates the same property expressions once in the same order and passes the same object contents. inflated?.byteLength ?? -1 and inflated === null ? -1 : inflated.byteLength agree because inflated has exactly Uint8Array | null and byteLength is always numeric. Nothing escapes, mutates, or changes parameter omission.
patches.whyNotUpstreamFirst: The object literals already receive the exact parameter context and the optional chain already has a numeric result in TypeScript. These ordinary target-neutral spellings avoid maintaining a copied WOFF reader while the emitter cannot compose Record and optional construction or retain the optional-chain value domain.
patches.verification: Targeted regeneration made woff_font.hpp compile independently and a C++ probe preserved the missing-decompressor null result plus diagnostic kind, origin, and table detail. Combining that candidate with the committed full structural-member table made all 17 package headers compile; the first named-Record trial exposed and the final typed-local spelling removed the optional-chain Any widening.
patches.unblocks: Makes woff_font.hpp compile, clearing open_type_glyph_outline_source.hpp and both package aggregators and moving @flighthq/font-formats from 13/17 to 17/17 when regenerated with the full SDK structural schema.
patches.expires: when the emitter materializes a contextual Record object literal before constructing an optional<Record> function argument, or Flight adopts the named bindings.

patches.refusal: assignment into a predeclared optional transition emits a present StructuralRef and then calls has_value on the payload
patches.rewrite: Chooses the transition index first, then performs one const array lookup and one existing undefined check.
patches.equivalence: For an active index both forms read and validate the same element. For a newly selected index getReadyTransitionIndex only returns an index from the same transitions array, so the added impossible-case check cannot alter a reachable result; state writes retain their order and the transition reference is read exactly once.
patches.whyNotUpstreamFirst: The source already narrows the optional binding, but the pinned emitter conflates the binding's optional storage with its present StructuralRef payload. A single post-branch binding is clearer TypeScript and avoids a whole-module override.
patches.verification: Targeted regeneration and focused compilation made statechart.hpp compile independently, moving the package from 1/5 to 2/5 before the separate guard override is applied.
patches.unblocks: Makes statechart.hpp compile. The companion complete guard override clears enable_statechart_guards.hpp and both aggregators.
patches.expires: when assignment and narrowing of an optional structural reference preserve one optional layer, or Flight adopts the single binding.

patches.refusal: imported ClipRegion.contours reads lose their nullable owner evidence, contextual null writes emit nullptr instead of optional absence, and loop-bounded contour reads lose dense-array presence
patches.rewrite: Adds one owner-side readClipRegionContours helper beside the ClipRegion declaration, snapshots each consumer read through it, obtains null through a private function with the exact number[][] | null return type, and marks length-bounded contour elements with TypeScript's erased non-null assertion.
patches.equivalence: The owner helper returns the same contours field once without copying; flight::Array copies preserve JavaScript array identity. noContours returns the same null primitive at each call. Flight documents ClipRegion as plain data, so snapshotting that declared field preserves the supported object model and every later read, branch, deep copy, and assignment. The non-null assertions emit no JavaScript, and each asserted index is proved by the immediately enclosing length guard or loop; malformed sparse JavaScript input still reaches the same member read and throws rather than being accepted or skipped. Existing interfaces, function signatures, field shapes, ordering, identity, absence, and version updates are unchanged; the new helper is additive.
patches.whyNotUpstreamFirst: These are ordinary target-neutral TypeScript spellings, and this repository already uses owner-side helpers where the emitter loses a declaration across a package barrel. They avoid a copied 850-line override while making the nullable field boundary and dense-index proofs explicit enough for every target.
patches.unblocks: Scoped regeneration moves @flighthq/clip from 3/4 to 4/4 emitted modules, restores all twelve absent functions, and makes clip_region.hpp compile independently with zero diagnostics. In the existing external angle consumer rive_clipping.hpp, all thirteen clip-origin diagnostics disappear; the header remains blocked by unrelated Rive/schema findings. Regenerating the 29-package scene2d-formats closure installs the three clip using declarations in svg_document.hpp, and focused compilation reports zero missing clip declarations at its real call sites.
patches.expires: when imported nullable property reads and contextual writes retain their declared union evidence and length-bounded dense array reads retain presence, or Flight adopts these explicit forms.
